page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d2s.20xlarge is a big data and storage-focused virtual instance operating on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by 80 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running on 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processors. The compute platform is paired with 352.0 GB of memory, supplying approximately 4.4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Networking throughput reaches a baseline network bandwidth of 35 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default.

The defining characteristic of ecs.d2s.20xlarge is its bundled local high-capacity storage subsystem, providing 235149 GB of integrated hard disk drive (HDD) capacity without dedicated GPU acceleration. The dense inclusion of mechanical storage offers high volumetric capacity per compute node, presenting significant qualitative cost efficiency for high-capacity ingestion and sequential access over network-attached alternatives. However, the use of spinning disks instead of solid-state drives entails typical rotational latency tradeoffs, prioritizing sequential throughput and raw storage density over random input/output operations per second.

Given the large storage volume, 80-core compute footprint, and 35 Gbps network interface, this instance fits data-intensive distributed analytics architectures. Primary deployment profiles include Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark clusters, distributed file systems, centralized log indexing platforms, and long-term batch ETL processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d2s.20xlarge is a dedicated big data compute instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 80 dedicated vCPUs alongside 352.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.4 GB RAM per core. A central feature is its massive bundled local storage allocation of 235149 GB across hard disk drives, paired with a 35 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators. The reliance on mechanical hard disk drives offers high storage capacity density, trading off low-latency random I/O for exceptional qualitative cost efficiency in large-scale sequential data persistence. This hardware footprint is engineered specifically for distributed data processing, making it well matched for Apache Hadoop clusters, large-scale batch ETL pipelines, distributed log retention platforms, and data lake storage nodes.
